issues.legal_issue: A later amendment expanding revisional jurisdiction does not apply to a decision that had become final before the amendment, absent a clear indication of retrospective operation.
material_facts: The appellate court had confirmed the trial court’s decision, and that appellate decision had become final subject only to the High Court’s limited revisional jurisdiction under the Code of Civil Procedure.
While the revision petition was pending, an amendment gave the High Court wider power to examine whether the appellate decision was according to law.
The amendment contained no indication that it was to operate retrospectively, but the High Court applied its expanded power and reversed the appellate decision.
issues.conclusion: The expanded revisional jurisdiction could not be applied to the already-final appellate decision. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the revision petition was remanded for decision under the limited jurisdiction on which it had been filed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 29(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, as amended, the High Court received revisional power wider than that available under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the absence of express words or necessary intendment, an enactment that takes away the finality of an existing decision or enlarges jurisdiction over it is not retrospective; such a change is substantive, not merely procedural or explanatory. This applies the principle in Colonial Sugar Refining Co. Ltd. v. Irving and Dafedar Niranjan Singh v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, and distinguishes Indira Sohan Lal v. Custodian of Evacuee Property and Moti Ram v. Suraj Bhan because in those cases the relevant decision had not become final before the change. Vora Abbasbhai Alimahomed v. Haji Gulamnabi Haji Safibhai describes the limits of the High Court’s jurisdiction under section 115 in this context.

rule.if: rent_appeal_revision and appellate_decision_final_before_later_law and later_law_expands_review_power and no_retroactive_intent

predicates.rent_appeal_revision: The proceeding is a revision arising from an appeal in a rent-control dispute.
predicates.appellate_decision_final_before_later_la: The appellate decision had become final, subject only to the previously available limited review, before the later law took effect.
predicates.later_law_expands_review_power: A later law gives the reviewing court broader power to examine the appellate decision than it previously had.
predicates.no_retroactive_intent: The later law contains no express or necessarily implied indication that the expanded power applies retrospectively.

issues.definition: When a rent-appeal revision concerns a decision already final before a later law expands review power, and that law shows no retrospective intent, the expanded power does not apply to that decision.
